name: Activity Attributes
purpose: Holds the details of each activity: its logical relationships, leads and lags, imposed dates, constraints, assumptions, resource needs, location and type of effort. The details are sometimes entered directly into the scheduling software, and otherwise collected on this form to help build the schedule model later. They are elaborated progressively as planning proceeds.

elements.guidance: A brief statement that summarizes the activity; it starts with a verb and is usually only a few words.
The activity described in enough detail that the people doing the work understand what is needed to complete it.
The predecessor activities that must happen before this activity, and the successor activities that cannot happen until after it.
The nature of the relationship between predecessor or successor and this activity, such as start-to-start, finish-to-start or finish-to-finish.
Any required delay between activities (lag) or acceleration (lead) that applies to the logical relationship.
Any required dates for start, completion, reviews or accomplishments.
Any limitation on the activity, such as finish-no-later-than dates, approaches to the work, or resources.
Any assumption about the activity, such as availability of resources, skill sets or others that affect it.

elements.printed_label: Number and Type of Team Resources Required | Skill Requirements
elements.guidance: The number and roles of the people needed, with the skill level such as junior or senior.
The materials, supplies or equipment needed to complete the activity.
The location, if the work is done somewhere other than the performing site.
Whether the work is fixed duration, fixed effort, level of effort, apportioned effort or another type.

tailoring: For some projects, enter the activities in the scheduling tool instead of keeping a separate set of activity attributes.
Include only the fields needed to manage the project effectively.
Constraints and assumptions can be recorded in the assumption log instead of on this form.
For an adaptive development approach, the activity list evolves as requirements are added or changed in the product backlog.
For an adaptive approach, consider adding a field for the planned release or iteration of each activity.
agile_or_adaptive: For adaptive approaches, or progressively elaborated projects, the attributes are updated throughout the project; add a release or iteration field per activity, since the list follows the product backlog (PDF pages 73 to 74, printed pages 62 to 63).

notes: printed_label joins several labels with " | " where one table row maps to more than one printed box. The blank form differs from Table 2.13 (PDF page 74, printed page 63): it prints one box "Imposed Dates or Other Constraints" for the table's two rows Imposed dates and Constraints, prints Type of Effort before Location of Performance, and uses Predecessors, Successor, Relationship and Lead or Lag columns for the three relationship rows. The printed labels win (references/fields/2.13.json). The logic table prints Relationship and Lead or Lag twice, once per side. The sheet is one per activity. The book's Tailoring Tips repeat the sentence about the activity list evolving with the backlog under the activity attributes; it is condensed once above. Process: 6.2 Define Activities.
